requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, including pagination

guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 for API access on behalf of a user. The narrowest documented applicable grant for reading project issues is read_api, which grants read access to the API including all groups and projects. The documented Issues API lists project issues with keyset or offset pagination. Account access to the target project remains a user prerequisite. Application registration, consent and token refresh are setup requirements, and nothing here has been tested.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

steps.title: Read issue titles from the first page of project issues
steps.detail: Documented scope is read_api, which grants read access to the API including all projects. The list endpoint for one project is GET /projects/:id/issues and returns paginated results. Private projects still require credentials. The title property is not yet evidenced on issue objects, so request fields are left empty until a citable source confirms it. Excluded: the api scope adds write access and is not needed; personal-token guidance does not transfer to OAuth. Boundary check: confirm only GET requests are sent and no issue create, update or delete call occurs.
steps.doneWhen: Unresolved until a citable source shows each issue object has a title property. Then the 200 JSON array of issues is read and the Link header is checked for rel=next. Boundary check: the outgoing log contains only GET requests to the project issues list and no create, update or delete calls.
